events.content:
I have optimized the partial pre-rendering (PPR) shell for the app. Previously, the `getDashboardData()` fetching was placed directly inside the main `Page` component, causing the entire page (including the static `

Dashboard

` shell) to be blocked while waiting for the data to resolve. I extracted the data-fetching logic and the components that depend on it (`CardStats`, `RevenueChart`, and `LatestInvoices`) into a new async `DashboardContent` component. Then, I updated the main `Page` component to be synchronous and wrapped `DashboardContent` in a `` boundary (reusing your `Loading` component as the fallback). As a result, Next.js can now immediately serve the static shell of your page (the `
` element and the `

`) while streaming the dynamic `DashboardContent` in the background.
